work: Each mole of Na2CO3 releases 2 mol Na+, so [Na2CO3] = 0.200 M / 2 = 0.100 M. In 0.2500 L this is n = 0.100 x 0.2500 = 0.02500 mol. Mass = 0.02500 mol x 105.99 g/mol = 2.65 g. Choice B (2.65 g) is the only match; doubling or halving again gives the 1.32 g or 5.30 g distractors.
rationale: Dividing the sodium ion concentration by the stoichiometric factor of 2 gives 0.100 M Na2CO3, and 0.02500 mol times 105.99 g/mol equals 2.65 g, which is choice B.
